package_info.package_versions: unknown (all distributed versions as of June 2020)
package_info.why_malicious: The GoldenSpy package is considered malicious because it contains a hidden backdoor that allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on systems where the tax software is installed. The backdoor operates independently of the main application, persists after uninstallation, and enables unauthorized remote access and control, representing a severe supply-chain compromise.

execution_context.file_location: GoldenSpy installation directory (separate executable or DLL)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The backdoor component runs as a separate process, connects to a remote C2 server, and executes arbitrary commands received from the attacker.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes a persistent connection to a remote command-and-control server, receives commands, executes them on the local system, and sends results back to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code creates an unauthorized remote access channel, allowing attackers to control the system without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate tax software should not include hidden remote access components or communicate with external servers for command execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools in enterprise environments, but only with explicit user consent and transparency.
key_indicators: Hidden persistent process independent of main application
Outbound network connections to unlisted remote servers
Ability to execute arbitrary code remotely

execution_context.file_location: GoldenSpy installation directory (remains after main app uninstall)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The backdoor remains installed and active even after the main tax software is uninstalled, continuing to run in the background.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After uninstallation, the code persists as a background process, maintaining remote access capabilities for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistence after uninstallation is a hallmark of malware, ensuring continued unauthorized access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should remove all components upon uninstallation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System management agents may persist, but with user awareness and consent.
key_indicators: No user notification of remaining components

attack_chain.action: User installs the official tax software, which silently deploys the GoldenSpy backdoor component.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor process is established and begins communication with C2 server.

attack_chain.action: Backdoor process connects to remote C2 server and awaits commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can remotely execute arbitrary code on the system.

attack_chain.action: User uninstalls the main tax software, but the backdoor remains active and continues to provide remote access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Continued unauthorized access and potential data exfiltration or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Background process establishing outbound connections to unlisted remote servers
Persistence of executables after main application uninstallation
Execution of arbitrary code received from network
file_indicators: Unknown executables or DLLs in the tax software installation directory
Files remaining after tax software uninstall
network_indicators: Outbound connections to hardcoded or suspicious C2 domains/IPs
Unusual traffic from tax software or related processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unknown or suspicious processes running from the tax software directory, especially those that persist after uninstallation. Inspect network traffic for connections to unlisted or suspicious remote servers. Check for executables or DLLs that remain after the main application is removed. Use endpoint detection tools to flag processes that execute commands received from the network.
